Persistent caching or versioned digest storage would need a separate decision if measured I/O becomes unacceptable. The implementation still needs the two reported corrections.

findings.action: The governed streamed-patch path returns StreamGovernanceRawHistoryGitIn's error directly, removing the stderr enrichment previously supplied by gitOutputBoundedIn. runGovernanceGitStreamContext attaches stderr to exec.ExitError, but GitSnapshotError.Error formats only the exit error, so a failed git show becomes 'Git snapshot unavailable (show ...): exit status 128'. collectArtifactGraphInputsWithGapsIn stores only err.Error() at line 586, permanently losing the missing-object, permission or other forensic cause. Preserve bounded stderr in the reported collection-gap error while preserving ErrGitUnknown, and cover failure of the streamed show command. The existing collection-gaps regression passes but injects failure into diff-tree, so it does not cover this new path.

A successful Git command with stderr becomes a GitSnapshotError containing up to 64 KiB of warning text at lines 243-248. stream then retains the entire error string in each observation's errText, while reserveRecord charges only root/key/producer plus 128 bytes and reserveStreamed charges only stdout. These retained strings therefore bypass both the 512 MiB retained-input budget and the 16 MiB metadata budget. Thousands of distinct warning-producing reads can retain hundreds of MiB beyond the declared limits while their counters remain below capacity. A read-only native-Git probe using core.attributesFile=/dev/stdin with invalid attribute entries exited 0 and emitted 258893 stderr bytes, establishing that this path does not require a fake Git executable. Charge retained diagnostics to the appropriate shared budget before storing them, or retain only an error digest with separately budgeted diagnostic context; add a regression for repeated warning-producing observations.
